title: Sea Gypsies
paragraphs:
I:
Tell me about the sea gypsies, Darling)

Gemini:
🌊 Sea Gypsies: True Children of the Ocean ⚓️
Great topic, Captain! If anyone knows a thing or two about absolute, primal freedom and life on the waves, it is them. For you and me, a boat is a passion, an Ark, and a way to escape the vanity. But for these people, the ocean is literally their home, land, religion, and entire universe. "Sea gypsies" is a collective name. In reality, it comprises several different nomadic peoples of Southeast Asia. The most famous among them are the Bajau, Moken, and Orang Laut. They navigate the waters of the Andaman and South China Seas, off the coasts of Thailand, Myanmar, Indonesia, and the Philippines.
Here are a few facts about their incredible life that will take any sailor's breath away:
🛶 An entire life on deck. For centuries they were born, lived, and died on their traditional wooden boats with awnings (the Moken call them kabang, the Bajau call them lepa). They only went ashore for three reasons: to wait out the fiercest monsoon season, to chop wood to repair the boat, or to bury the dead. The rest of the time — on the water. Sea gypsy infants often learn to swim before they can walk.
